metadata.name: bg
metadata.displayName: bg - Resume a job in the background
metadata.description: Move a stopped job to the background

installation.note: bg is a shell built-in (commonly in bash), not a standalone binary

overview.summary: The bg command resumes a stopped job and runs it in the background. It works with job control in your shell (like bash), typically after you suspend a program with Ctrl+Z.
when_to_use: You suspended a program with Ctrl+Z and want it to continue in the background
You want to keep using the terminal while a job runs
You are managing multiple interactive jobs in one terminal

syntax.description: If JOB_SPEC is omitted, bg operates on the current job. JOB_SPEC is often like %1, %2, etc., shown by the jobs command.

examples.title: Suspend and continue a job in the background
examples.description: Suspend a running command, then resume it in the background
examples.use_case: Keep a long-running task going while freeing your prompt

examples.title: Resume a specific job by number
examples.description: Resume job number 2 in the background

common_pitfalls.issue: No job control in the current shell/session
common_pitfalls.description: In some non-interactive shells or restricted environments, job control may be disabled.
common_pitfalls.solution: Run an interactive shell (e.g., bash) or ensure job control is enabled for your session.

common_pitfalls.issue: Background jobs still write to the terminal
common_pitfalls.description: A background job can still output to the terminal and interrupt your typing.
common_pitfalls.solution: Redirect output (e.g., command > out.txt 2>&1 &) or use disown/nohup when appropriate.

related_commands.description: Bring a background/stopped job to the foreground
